ops.title: present the full plan and get approval before code changes — \"continue\" mid-incident or a plan-mode exit is not blanket approval to implement
ops.body:
2026-07-03, mid-incident: after the user exited plan mode and said "Continue", I started
editing fusekit directly. The user interrupted: "stop, re-enter plan mode, undo the changes you
just did, and present the plan to me instead of just going ahead. make sure to undo manually
and not interfere with other changes."

**Why:** exiting plan mode (or an urgent "continue") signals *keep working the problem*, not
*skip plan approval*. For multi-repo, release-grade, or shared-library changes this user wants
the plan presented via ExitPlanMode first — even during an active incident. Design pushback is
also cheap at plan time (here: "find a more appropriate priority" flipped delete-the-demotion
into `nice 5`).

**How to apply:** finish planning and get ExitPlanMode approval before any working-tree edit.
When asked to undo: reverse each of my edits by hand and restore my deletions byte-exact
(`git show HEAD:path > path`) — never broad `git checkout`/`jj restore` that could clobber
concurrent-session changes ([[never-revert-user-working-tree-edits]]) — then verify with
`git status`/`diff` that the tree matches pristine.
